qe: During the 19th century, a regressive social custom under the name of 'Kulinism' heavily degraded the position of women through institutionalized polygamy and mismatched marriages. This system was predominantly prevalent in which region of India?
qh: 19वीं शताब्दी के दौरान, 'कुलीनवाद' (Kulinism) नाम से प्रचलित एक प्रतिगामी सामाजिक प्रथा ने संस्थागत बहुविवाह और बेमेल विवाहों के माध्यम से महिलाओं की स्थिति को भारी ठेस पहुँचाई। यह व्यवस्था मुख्य रूप से भारत के किस क्षेत्र में प्रचलित थी?
o: Bengal
Madras Presidency
Punjab
Maharashtra
e: Detailed Explanation: In 19th-century Bengal, under the social system of Kulinism, highly exploitative forms of polygamy were practiced. Under this custom, even elderly men belonging to upper castes married very young girls, often leaving them abandoned or destitute, which severely degraded the overall position of women.

qe: Which prominent early socio-religious reformer explicitly challenged orthodox clerical groups by condemning the practice of Sati as a 'murder according to every shastra'?
qh: किस प्रमुख प्रारंभिक सामाजिक-धार्मिक सुधारक ने सती प्रथा की स्पष्ट रूप से 'प्रत्येक शास्त्र के अनुसार हत्या' के रूप में निंदा करके रूढ़िवादी लिपिकीय समूहों को चुनौती दी थी?
o: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
Raja Rammohan Roy
Dayanand Saraswati
Mahadev Govind Ranade
e: Detailed Explanation: Raja Rammohan Roy was the pioneering reformer of modern India who led a historic campaign against the practice of Sati. He used scriptural analysis to fight orthodox opposition, explicitly stating that the forced immolation of widows was nothing short of a 'murder according to every shastra'.

qe: The rigid stratification and social segregation associated with the caste system in modern India created major barriers against which democratic development?
qh: आधुनिक भारत में जाति व्यवस्था से जुड़े कड़े स्तरीकरण और सामाजिक अलगाव ने किस लोकतांत्रिक विकास के खिलाफ प्रमुख बाधाएं पैदा कीं?
o: The growth of a united national feeling and democratic spirit
The introduction of land revenue collection frameworks
The establishing of cross-border maritime trading networks
The direct legal translation of Western scientific texts
e: Detailed Explanation: The rigid caste system in India checked social mobility, checked individual initiative, and splintered society into numerous fragmented groups based on ritual status. In modern times, this fragmentation became a major structural obstacle to the development of a united national feeling and the spread of democracy.

qe: The dissemination of colonial culture and ideology as the dominant current by British rule triggered a reactive cultural movement among 19th-century Indian intellectuals. This response was characterized by:
qh: ब्रिटिश शासन द्वारा औपनिवेशिक संस्कृति और विचारधारा के प्रसार ने 19वीं शताब्दी के भारतीय बुद्धिजीवियों के बीच एक प्रतिक्रियात्मक सांस्कृतिक आंदोलन को जन्म दिया। इस प्रतिक्रिया की विशेषता क्या थी?
o: An immediate and total legal conversion to Western religious practices
An attempt to reinvigorate traditional institutions and realize the potential of traditional culture
The total abandonment of scriptural studies across all local languages
A spontaneous mass migration toward non-colonized European territories
e: Detailed Explanation: Faced with the challenge of an intrusive colonial culture and ideology, enlightened Indian thinkers did not blindly accept Westernization. Instead, they sought to reinvigorate traditional institutions, purge them of social evils, and realize the true reforming potential of traditional culture.

qe: What primary realization catalyzed the shared conviction among English-educated Indian youth in the late 19th century to reform their own socio-religious structures?
qh: 19वीं शताब्दी के उत्तरार्ध में अंग्रेजी-शिक्षित भारतीय युवाओं के बीच अपने स्वयं के सामाजिक-धार्मिक ढांचों में सुधार करने के साझा विश्वास को किस प्राथमिक अहसास ने प्रेरित किया?
o: The awareness that India was colonized due to internal weaknesses within its own social structure and culture
The absolute lack of rich mineral reservoirs in the sub-Himalayan zones
The dynamic degradation of linear agricultural productivity indices
The sudden structural breakdown of natural wildlife biomes
e: Detailed Explanation: The impact of modern Western ideas and the reality of defeat by a foreign power made educated Indians introspect. They realized that a vast country like India had been colonized by a handful of foreigners primarily because of deep structural weaknesses, superstitions, and social fragmentation within the Indian society and culture, which highlighted the urgent need for internal reform.

qe: During the 19th century, social reformers initially linked social movements directly with religious reforms. What was the primary reason for this close structural linkage?
qh: 19वीं शताब्दी के दौरान, सामाजिक सुधारकों ने शुरू में सामाजिक आंदोलनों को सीधे धार्मिक सुधारों से जोड़ा। इस करीबी संरचनात्मक जुड़ाव का प्राथमिक कारण क्या था?
o: Nearly all social ills like untouchability and gender inequality derived institutional legitimacy from religion
The colonial government mandated that all social changes must be cleared by religious bodies
Indian languages lacked secular terms to propagate ideas to the lower strata of society
The early upper-class reformers aimed to establish a new monotheistic state religion legally
e: Detailed Explanation: Social reform movements were initially tied to religion because major social evils, including untouchability and gender-based discrimination, derived their validation, authority, and structural legitimacy from misinterpreted religious traditions and scriptures.

qe: Which of the following organizations was among the earliest institutional setups instrumental in spearheading social reforms in India before the national movement took over leadership in the 20th century?
qh: 20वीं शताब्दी में राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन द्वारा नेतृत्व संभालने से पहले, भारत में सामाजिक सुधारों का नेतृत्व करने में सहायक शुरुआती संस्थागत सेटअपों में से कौन सा संगठन शामिल था?
o: The Indian National Social Conference
The All India Scheduled Castes Federation
The Congress Khilafat Swaraj Party
The Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha
e: Detailed Explanation: In the initial stages, localized organizations such as the Indian National Social Conference, the Servants of India Society, Christian missionaries, and enlightened individuals laid the foundation for social reform long before the Indian National Congress adopted it on a mass scale.

qe: To effectively reach and mobilize the masses, 19th-century socio-religious reformers primarily relied on which communicative tool?
qh: जनता तक प्रभावी ढंग से पहुँचने और उन्हें लामबंद करने के लिए, 19वीं शताब्दी के सामाजिक-धार्मिक सुधारक मुख्य रूप से किस संचार साधन पर निर्भर थे?
o: English-only political pamphlets distributed to the intelligentsia
Indian vernacular languages propagated through literature, press, and drama
Direct legal appeals filed inside the Federal Privy Council channels
Spontaneous radio broadcasts managed from non-colonial European centers
e: Detailed Explanation: Reformers recognized that westernized media was confined to the upper classes. To penetrate the lower strata, they actively used Indian vernacular languages and multiple formats—novels, dramas, poetry, short stories, and the local press.

qe: The comprehensive agenda of the early socio-religious reform movements in India was fundamentally anchored on which two-point core objective?
qh: भारत में शुरुआती सामाजिक-धार्मिक सुधार आंदोलनों का व्यापक एजेंडा मुख्य रूप से किन दो बिंदुओं के मुख्य उद्देश्य पर आधारित था?
o: Betterment of the status of women and removal of disabilities arising out of untouchability
The absolute expansion of private land sales and total abolition of local panchayats
Promoting Western dress codes and implementing English-only educational test metrics
Securing military representations for native intermediate castes inside colonial setups
e: Detailed Explanation: Although the reform movements covered many diverse aspects, their core agenda focused on two major areas: improving the status and rights of women in society, and eliminating the disabilities arising from untouchability.

qe: In the 19th century, Muslim women under Islamic legal traditions possessed what specific property right compared to their contemporary Hindu counterparts?
qh: 19वीं शताब्दी में, इस्लामी कानूनी परंपराओं के तहत मुस्लिम महिलाओं के पास उनकी समकालीन हिंदू महिलाओं की तुलना में कौन सा विशिष्ट संपत्ति का अधिकार था?
o: They could inherit property, but only half as much as men could
They enjoyed complete absolute equality with men in inheriting full agricultural holdings
They were legally barred from owning any physical real estate asset entirely
They could inherit property only if they terminated their existing marriage lines
e: Detailed Explanation: Unlike 19th-century Hindu women who lacked the right to inherit property, Muslim women could inherit property under Islamic law. However, gender inequality remained, as they were legally entitled to inherit only half as much share as men could.

qe: Social reformers actively targeted reforms in the domestic sphere, arguing that a radical change in the household was essential because:
qh: सामाजिक सुधारकों ने घरेलू क्षेत्र (domestic sphere) में सुधारों को सक्रिय रूप से लक्षित किया, यह तर्क देते हुए कि घर में आमूल-चूल परिवर्तन आवश्यक था क्योंकि:
o: The initial socialization of individuals takes place in the home, where women play a crucial role
The colonial government offered financial subsidies only to reformed households
The domestic sphere was the primary source of state agricultural tax collections
They aimed to completely eliminate traditional family structures in favor of Western systems
e: Detailed Explanation: Reformers understood that the domestic sphere is where the initial socialization of individuals occurs. Because women play a central role in rearing children, transforming the domestic environment was seen as key to shaping reformed citizens.

qe: When launching a frontal attack against the practice of Sati, Raja Rammohan Roy and his followers used which argument to strengthen their appeal?
qh: सती प्रथा के खिलाफ मोर्चा खोलते समय राजा राममोहन राय और उनके अनुयायियों ने अपने आह्वान को मजबूत करने के लिए किस तर्क का इस्तेमाल किया?
o: They argued that true religion and scriptures did not sanction an inferior status or forced death for women
They appealed to the financial benefits that British landlords would gain from widow estates
They stated that the practice was imported recently from non-Asian colonial systems
They advocated that the custom should be restricted strictly to lower castes
e: Detailed Explanation: To counter orthodox opposition, Raja Rammohan Roy turned to scripture. He argued from a rationalist perspective that the true, uncorrupted core of religion did not support an inferior status or the forced immolation of widows, describing it as a violation of human dignity.

qe: The historic anti-Sati regulation enacted under Lord William Bentinck, which declared the custom illegal and punishable as culpable homicide, was formally designated as:
qh: लॉर्ड विलियम बेंटिक के तहत अधिनियमित ऐतिहासिक सती-विरोधी नियम, जिसने इस प्रथा को अवैध और आपराधिक मानव वध के रूप में दंडनीय घोषित किया, उसे औपचारिक रूप से क्या कहा गया था?
o: Regulation XVII, A.D. 1829 of the Bengal Code
Bengal Infanticide Restriction Act of 1795
Native Civil Marriage Act of 1872
Age of Consent Code, 1891
e: Detailed Explanation: The practice was declared illegal and punishable by criminal courts as culpable homicide under Regulation XVII, A.D. 1829 of the Bengal Code. Initially applicable to the Bengal Presidency, it was extended to Madras and Bombay in 1830.

qe: In 1870, the colonial government passed a specific legislative Act targeting the secret practice of female infanticide. What did this Act make compulsory for parents?
qh: 1870 में, औपनिवेशिक सरकार ने कन्या भ्रूण हत्या/शिशु हत्या की गुप्त प्रथा को लक्षित करते हुए एक विशिष्ट अधिनियम पारित किया। इस अधिनियम ने माता-पिता के लिए क्या अनिवार्य कर दिया?
o: The mandatory registration of the birth of all babies and subsequent verification of female infants
The compulsory enrollment of all female children into Christian missionary boarding facilities
Paying a direct metabolic tax surcharge to the local district revenue collectorate
Surrendering ownership of all ancestral property to female heirs immediately
e: Detailed Explanation: To combat female infanticide practiced in secrecy among certain upper classes, the Female Infanticide Prevention Act of 1870 made it compulsory for parents to register all births and introduced verification checks on female infants for several years.

qe: The enactment of the landmark Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856, which legalised widow remarriage and legitimized their issues, was primarily due to the relentless efforts of which scholar?
qh: ऐतिहासिक हिंदू विधवा पुनर्विवाह अधिनियम, 1856 का पारित होना, जिसने विधवा विवाह को वैध बनाया, मुख्य रूप से किस विद्वान के अथक प्रयासों के कारण हुआ था?
o: Pandit Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
Raja Rammohan Roy
Karsondas Mulji
Professor D.K. Karve
e: Detailed Explanation: Pandit Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, serving as the principal of Sanskrit College in Calcutta, led the campaign for widow remarriage. He famously cited Vedic texts to prove to the orthodox community that Hindu traditions originally permitted the practice.

qe: Who among the following reformers established the specialized journal 'Satya Prakash' in Gujarati in 1852 to advocate for the right of widow remarriage?
qh: निम्नलिखित सुधारकों में से किसने विधवा पुनर्विवाह के अधिकार की वकालत करने के लिए 1852 में गुजराती में 'सत्य प्रकाश' (Satya Prakash) पत्रिका की शुरुआत की थी?
o: Karsondas Mulji
Vishnu Shastri Pandit
Veerasalingam Pantulu
B.M. Malabari
e: Detailed Explanation: Karsondas Mulji was a pioneering reformer who used journalism for social change. In 1852, he launched the Gujarati weekly 'Satya Prakash' to challenge orthodox practices and advocate for widow remarriage in western India.

qe: Professor D.K. Karve made outstanding structural contributions to the upliftment of high-caste Hindu widows in western India. Which practical measure did he initiate in Poona?
qh: प्रोफेसर डी.के. कर्वे ने पश्चिमी भारत में उच्च जाति की हिंदू विधवाओं के उत्थान में उत्कृष्ट योगदान दिया। उन्होंने पूना में कौन सा व्यावहारिक कदम शुरू किया?
o: He opened a dedicated widows' home providing facilities for vocational training
He introduced an aggressive legal suit inside the local high court against the priestly class
He completely banned the entry of lower castes into local standard schooling spaces
He established the first native maritime shipping company managed by women
e: Detailed Explanation: Professor D.K. Karve dedicated his life to the welfare of widows. He opened a widows' home in Poona to provide high-caste widows with shelter, education, and vocational training, helping them achieve independence and purpose.

qe: The Native Marriage Act (or Civil Marriage Act) of 1872 introduced legislative restrictions against child marriage, but it had a limited impact across India because:
qh: 1872 के नेटिव मैरिज एक्ट (या सिविल मैरिज एक्ट) ने बाल विवाह के खिलाफ विधायी प्रतिबंध पेश किए, लेकिन भारत भर में इसका सीमित प्रभाव पड़ा क्योंकि:
o: The Act was explicitly not applicable to Hindus, Muslims, and other recognized mainstream faiths
The colonial judiciary struck down the entire regulation as unconstitutional within a year
It raised the legal marriage age artificially to an unmanageable baseline of 25 years
The law was enforceable only within the remote limits of the Madras Presidency
e: Detailed Explanation: The Native Marriage Act of 1872 prohibited child marriage and permitted inter-caste marriages, but its scope was extremely narrow because it did not apply to Hindus, Muslims, or other major established religious faiths.

qe: The relentless efforts of the Parsi reformer B.M. Malabari directly culminated in the enactment of which piece of colonial legislation that prohibited the marriage of girls below the age of 12?
qh: पारसी सुधारक बी.एम. मालाबारी के अथक प्रयासों के परिणामस्वरूप कौन सा औपनिवेशिक कानून लागू हुआ, जिसने 12 वर्ष से कम उम्र की लड़कियों के विवाह को प्रतिबंधित कर दिया?
o: Age of Consent Act, 1891
Sarda Act, 1930
Native Marriage Act, 1872
Child Marriage Restraint Amendment Act, 1978
e: Detailed Explanation: B.M. Malabari campaigned vigorously against child marriage and the treatment of child widows. His efforts led to the passage of the Age of Consent Act in 1891, which raised the legal age of consent for marriage for girls to 12 years.

qe: The highly influential Sarda Act of 1930 pushed up the minimum legal marriage age boundaries across British India to which standard parameters?
qh: 1930 के अत्यधिक प्रभावशाली शारदा अधिनियम (Sarda Act) ने ब्रिटिश भारत में न्यूनतम कानूनी विवाह आयु सीमा को बढ़ाकर कितना कर दिया था?
o: 18 years for boys and 14 years for girls
21 years for boys and 18 years for girls
16 years for boys and 12 years for girls
20 years for boys and 15 years for girls
e: Detailed Explanation: The Child Marriage Restraint Act of 1929 (popularly known as the Sarda Act after its sponsor Rai Sahib Harbilas Sarda), which came into effect in 1930, fixed the minimum legal marriage age at 18 years for boys and 14 years for girls.

qe: Which educational institution, established in Calcutta in 1849, is recognized as the first major fruit of the powerful movement for women's higher education in India?
qh: 1849 में कलकत्ता में स्थापित कौन सा शैक्षणिक संस्थान, भारत में महिलाओं की उच्च शिक्षा के शक्तिशाली आंदोलन के पहले प्रमुख परिणाम के रूप में मान्यता प्राप्त है?
o: The Bethune School, founded by J.E.D. Bethune
The Calcutta Female Juvenile Society
The Lady Hardinge Medical College
The Indian Women’s University
e: Detailed Explanation: The Bethune School, founded in 1849 by John Elliot Drinkwater Bethune (President of the Council of Education), was a milestone. It was the first secular school for girls in India and triggered a broader movement for female education.

qe: Apart from his pioneering role in scriptural analysis for widow remarriage, Pandit Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was actively associated as an organizer with how many girls' schools in Bengal?
qh: विधवा पुनर्विवाह के लिए शास्त्रीय विश्लेषण में अपनी अग्रणी भूमिका के अलावा, पंडित ईश्वर चंद्र विद्यासागर बंगाल में कितने लड़कियों के स्कूलों के आयोजक के रूप में सक्रिय रूप से जुड़े हुए थे?
o: No less than 35 girls' schools
Exactly 5 girls' schools
More than 100 girls' schools
Strictly 12 girls' schools
e: Detailed Explanation: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a passionate advocate for female literacy. In his capacity as a government inspector of schools, he used his position and personal funds to organize and establish no less than 35 girls' schools across Bengal.

qe: Which landmark historical document on educational policy explicitly laid great structural stress on the urgent need for female education in British India in 1854?
qh: शिक्षा नीति पर किस ऐतिहासिक दस्तावेज़ ने 1854 में ब्रिटिश भारत में महिला शिक्षा की तत्काल आवश्यकता पर विशेष संरचनात्मक बल दिया था?
o: Charles Wood’s Despatch on Education
Macaulay’s Minute on Indian Education
The Hunter Commission Report
The Raleigh University Commission Guidelines
e: Detailed Explanation: Sir Charles Wood's Despatch on Education of 1854, often called the 'Magna Carta of English Education in India', explicitly highlighted the importance of female education and recommended government grants to support girls' schools.

qe: The outstanding institution known as the 'Indian Women’s University', which provided specialized higher education infrastructure to women, was set up in 1916 by which reformer?
qh: महिलाओं को विशेष उच्च शिक्षा बुनियादी ढांचा प्रदान करने वाले 'इंडियन विमेंस यूनिवर्सिटी' (Indian Women's University) की स्थापना 1916 में किस सुधारक द्वारा की गई थी?
o: Professor D.K. Karve
Ramabai Ranade
Sarla Devi Chaudhurani
Pandita Ramabai Saraswati
e: Detailed Explanation: In 1916, Professor D.K. Karve established the Indian Women's University (now known as SNDT Women's University) in Pune, marking a historic milestone as the first university dedicated exclusively to women in India.

qe: During the opening decades of the twentieth century, which mass political events served as the primary liberating experience for otherwise home-centered Indian women?
qh: बीसवीं शताब्दी के शुरुआती दशकों के दौरान, किन जन-राजनीतिक घटनाओं ने मुख्य रूप से घरेलू स्तर पर केंद्रित भारतीय महिलाओं के लिए प्राथमिक मुक्ति के अनुभव के रूप में कार्य किया?
o: Participation in the Swadeshi, anti-partition, and Home Rule movements
Attending secret commercial banking tracking seminars in Bombay
Filing joint civil lawsuits against local village panchayats
Enrolling into newly opened British military administrative services
e: Detailed Explanation: Entering the public sphere during the Swadeshi (1905), anti-partition, and Home Rule movements marked a major turning point for Indian women. They stepped out of domestic isolation to join processions, picket shops, and engage in political activism.

qe: The organization named 'Bharat Stree Mahamandal', which held its first historical meeting in Allahabad in 1910, was founded by which prominent woman leader?
qh: 1910 में इलाहाबाद में अपनी पहली ऐतिहासिक बैठक आयोजित करने वाले 'भारत स्त्री महामंडल' (Bharat Stree Mahamandal) नामक संगठन की स्थापना किस प्रमुख महिला नेता द्वारा की गई थी?
o: Sarla Devi Chaudhurani
Ramabai Ranade
Pandita Ramabai
Sarojini Naidu
e: Detailed Explanation: Sarla Devi Chaudhurani convened the first meeting of the Bharat Stree Mahamandal in Allahabad in 1910. It is widely considered the first major pan-Indian women's organization established by a woman, aimed at promoting female education and abolishing the purdah system.

qe: The prominent 'Ladies Social Conference' (Bharat Mahila Parishad) was founded in 1904 in Bombay as a specialized wing under the structural guidance of which parent body?
qh: प्रसिद्ध 'लेडीज सोशल कॉन्फ्रेंस' (भारत महिला परिषद) की स्थापना 1904 में बॉम्बे में किस मूल संस्था के संरचनात्मक मार्गदर्शन में एक विशेष शाखा के रूप में की गई थी?
o: The National Social Conference
The Brahmo Samaj Core Council
The Arya Mahila Samaj
The All India Women’s Conference
e: Detailed Explanation: Ramabai Ranade founded the Ladies Social Conference (Bharat Mahila Parishad) in 1904 in Bombay. It operated as a specialized branch under the aegis of the National Social Conference, focusing on targeted social reforms for women.

qe: The 'All India Women’s Conference' (AIWC), recognized as one of the first major women's organizations with an egalitarian approach, was founded in 1927 by whom?
qh: एक समतावादी दृष्टिकोण (egalitarian approach) के साथ पहले प्रमुख महिला संगठनों में से एक के रूप में मान्यता प्राप्त 'अखिल भारतीय महिला सम्मेलन' (AIWC) की स्थापना 1927 में किसके द्वारा की गई थी?
o: Margaret Cousins
Sarla Devi Chaudhurani
Mehribai Tata
Cornelia Sorabji
e: Detailed Explanation: The All India Women’s Conference (AIWC) was founded by Margaret Cousins in 1927. Its first conference was hosted at Fergusson College, Pune, with founding members including Sarojini Naidu and Kamladevi Chattopadhyaya.

qe: Which of the following objective principles formed the core constitutional vision of the All India Women’s Conference (AIWC) when it expanded its platform in 1927?
qh: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा उद्देश्य सिद्धांत अखिल भारतीय महिला सम्मेलन (AIWC) के मुख्य संवैधानिक दृष्टिकोण का हिस्सा था जब उसने 1927 में अपने मंच का विस्तार किया था?
o: To work for a society based on principles of social justice, integrity, equal rights, and opportunities
To enforce the strict insulation of intermediate caste tracking across legislatures
To structurally support the retention of the medieval purdah status systems
To dynamically channelize land ownership exclusively to wealthy banking families
e: Detailed Explanation: The AIWC was built on an egalitarian philosophy. Its stated goals were to fight for a society rooted in social justice, integrity, equal rights, and opportunities, ensuring the essentials of life were distributed based on fairness rather than accident of birth or sex.

qe: The rigid structural concept of Hindu 'chaturvarnashrama' dictated that a person's caste status systematically determined which social privileges before birth?
qh: हिंदू 'चातुर्वर्णश्रम' की कठोर संरचनात्मक अवधारणा यह निर्देशित करती थी कि किसी व्यक्ति की जाति की स्थिति जन्म से पहले ही किन सामाजिक विशेषाधिकारों को व्यवस्थित रूप से निर्धारित करती थी?
o: Access to education, land ownership, profession, and sources of drinking water
The precise volume of international maritime import trade parameters
Direct baseline tracking metrics of judicial high court appeals
The structural layout of currency print velocity values inside local markets
e: Detailed Explanation: Under the rigid chaturvarnashrama framework, caste dictated almost every aspect of an individual's social life before birth—including access to education, ownership of landed property, professional pursuits, sources of drinking water, and temple entry rules.

qe: How did the introduction of British administrative and legal measures indirectly deal a severe blow to traditional caste-based inequalities in India?
qh: ब्रिटिश प्रशासनिक और कानूनी उपायों की शुरूआत ने अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से भारत में पारंपरिक जाति-आधारित असमानताओं को कैसे गहरा झटका दिया?
o: By introducing the concept of equality before law in a uniformly applied system of law and stripping caste panchayats of judicial functions
By legally forcing all intermediate castes to engage in uniform agricultural vocations
By mandating that scriptural studies must be cleared by British military tribunals
By entirely freezing urban mobility and eliminating private property in land
e: Detailed Explanation: The British administration introduced a uniform legal system based on the principle of equality before the law. By removing judicial powers from traditional caste panchayats and opening administrative services to all castes on secular lines, it structurally undermined old caste hierarchies.

qe: Mahatma Gandhi launched a comprehensive national crusade to eradicate untouchability root and branch. Which specialized organization did he establish in 1932 to advance this cause?
qh: महात्मा गांधी ने अस्पृश्यता को जड़ से खत्म करने के लिए एक व्यापक राष्ट्रीय अभियान शुरू किया। इस उद्देश्य को आगे बढ़ाने के लिए उन्होंने 1932 में किस विशेष संगठन की स्थापना की?
o: All India Harijan Sangh
Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha
All India Scheduled Castes Federation
Self-Respect Movement Front
e: Detailed Explanation: Anchoring his campaign on humanism and reason, Mahatma Gandhi founded the All India Harijan Sangh in 1932 to combat untouchability and launched the weekly publication 'Harijan' to advocate for the civil rights of the depressed classes.

qe: In Maharashtra, the powerful anti-caste movement challenging Brahminical domination and prioritizing lower-caste and female literacy was spearheaded by which iconic reformer?
qh: महाराष्ट्र में, ब्राह्मणवादी वर्चस्व को चुनौती देने वाले और निचली जाति तथा महिला साक्षरता को प्राथमिकता देने वाले शक्तिशाली जाति-विरोधी आंदोलन का नेतृत्व किस प्रसिद्ध सुधारक ने किया था?
o: Jyotiba Phule
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
The Maharaja of Kolhapur
Ramabai Ranade
e: Detailed Explanation: Jyotiba Phule, born into a low-caste Mali family, led a historic movement against upper-caste hegemony in Maharashtra. He prioritized education for the lower strata and established several pioneering schools for girls and lower-caste children.

qe: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar led the historic 'Mahad Satyagraha' in March 1927. What specific civil right was targeted during this public demonstration?
qh: डॉ. बी.आर. अंबेडकर ने मार्च 1927 में ऐतिहासिक 'महाद सत्याग्रह' (Mahad Satyagraha) का नेतृत्व किया था। इस सार्वजनिक प्रदर्शन के दौरान किस विशिष्ट नागरिक अधिकार को लक्षित किया गया था?
o: The right of untouchables to draw water from the public Chawdar tank
Securing separate political representation parameters inside local district boards
Forcing the colonial judiciary to completely ban the free sale of land
Demanding the immediate closure of all high-cost British educational facilities
e: Detailed Explanation: The Mahad Satyagraha of March 1927 was an iconic civil rights campaign led by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. He led a procession of thousands of untouchables to the Chawdar tank in Mahad to assert their right to use a public water source that had historically been denied to them by orthodox caste groups.

qe: The specialized organization named 'Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha', which operated under the transformative motto 'Educate, Agitate and Organise', was established in 1924 by whom?
qh: परिवर्तनकारी आदर्श वाक्य 'शिक्षित करो, संघर्ष करो और संगठित बनो' (Educate, Agitate and Organise) के तहत काम करने वाले 'बहिष्कृत हितकारिणी सभा' (Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha) की स्थापना 1924 में किसके द्वारा की गई थी?
o: Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar
Jyotiba Phule
E.V. Ramaswamy Naicker
Sri Narayana Guru
e: Detailed Explanation: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar founded the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha in Bombay in 1924. The organization was designed to bring the grievances of Dalits to the government's attention, promote education, and improve their socio-economic conditions under the banner: 'Educate, Agitate and Organise'.

qe: In 1814, Raja Rammohan Roy established an early promotional platform in Calcutta to campaign against idolatry, caste rigidities, and meaningless rituals. What was the name of this organization?
qh: 1814 में, राजा राममोहन राय ने मूर्तिपूजा, जातिगत कठोरता और निरर्थक कर्मकांडों के खिलाफ अभियान चलाने के लिए कलकत्ता में एक प्रारंभिक मंच की स्थापना की थी। इस संगठन का नाम क्या था?
o: Atmiya Sabha
Tattvabodhini Sabha
Paramahansa Mandali
Manav Dharma Sabha
e: Detailed Explanation: Raja Rammohan Roy founded the Atmiya Sabha (Society of Friends) in Calcutta in 1814 to propagate the monotheistic ideals of the Vedanta and to challenge social evils.

qe: Raja Rammohan Roy published a strategic theological treatise in 1820 where he attempted to separate the moral and philosophical message of the New Testament from its miracle stories. What was the title of this work?
qh: राजा राममोहन राय ने 1820 में एक रणनीतिक धार्मिक ग्रंथ प्रकाशित किया, जिसमें उन्होंने न्यू टेस्टामेंट (New Testament) के नैतिक और दार्शनिक संदेश को उसकी चमत्कारिक कहानियों से अलग करने का प्रयास किया। इस कृति का शीर्षक क्या था?
o: Precepts of Jesus
Gift to Monotheists
Tattvabodhini Patrika
Satya Prakash
e: Detailed Explanation: In his work 'Precepts of Jesus' (1820), Raja Rammohan Roy praised the moral and philosophical message of the New Testament while separating it from miracle stories, which earned him the ire of Christian missionaries.

qe: The long-term reformative agenda of the Brahmo Samaj, which focused on purifying Hinduism and preaching monotheism, was anchored fundamentally on which two pillars?
qh: हिंदू धर्म को शुद्ध करने और एकेश्वरवाद का उपदेश देने पर केंद्रित ब्रह्म समाज का दीर्घकालिक सुधार एजेंडा मौलिक रूप से किन दो स्तंभों पर आधारित था?
o: Reason and the Vedas/Upanishads
Divine Avataras and Karma
Bhakti cult and Blind faith
Western sciences and Puranas
e: Detailed Explanation: The baseline working strategy of the Brahmo Samaj was structurally anchored on the twin pillars of human reason and the ancient teachings of the Vedas and Upanishads.

qe: Which orthodox socio-cultural organization was explicitly founded by Raja Radhakant Deb to counter the progressive socio-religious propaganda of the Brahmo Samaj?
qh: ब्रह्म समाज के प्रगतिशील सामाजिक-धार्मिक प्रचार का मुकाबला करने के लिए राजा राधाकांत देव द्वारा किस रूढ़िवादी सामाजिक-सांस्कृतिक संगठन की स्थापना की गई थी?
o: Dharma Sabha
Tattvabodhini Sabha
Paramahansa Sabha
Atmiya Sabha
e: Detailed Explanation: To oppose the anti-idolatry and progressive steps of Raja Rammohan Roy, Raja Radhakant Deb organized the 'Dharma Sabha' as an orthodox counter-front.

qe: Raja Rammohan Roy took specific progressive stances on macroeconomic and land revenue issues. Which of the following fields reflects his economic demands under the British Raj?
qh: राजा राममोहन राय ने समष्टि अर्थशास्त्र और भूमि राजस्व के मुद्दों पर प्रगतिशील रुख अपनाया। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा क्षेत्र ब्रिटिश राज के तहत उनकी आर्थिक मांगों को दर्शाता है?
o: Fixation of maximum rents for Bengali zamindars and reduction of export duties on Indian goods abroad
The total privatization of all tax-free lands in rural Bengal
An immediate implementation of high export tariffs on native manufacturing units
The absolute expansion of the East India Company's exclusive monopoly trading rights
e: Detailed Explanation: As a political activist, Roy condemned the oppressive practices of Bengali zamindars, demanded the fixation of maximum rents, called for a reduction of export duties on Indian goods abroad, and sought the abolition of the East India Company's trading rights.

qe: Before informally integrating with the Brahmo Samaj in 1842 to give it a new lease of life, Maharishi Debendranath Tagore headed which systematic study platform established in 1839?
qh: 1842 में ब्रह्म समाज के साथ अनौपचारिक रूप से जुड़ने से पहले, महर्षि देवेंद्रनाथ टैगोर ने 1839 में स्थापित किस व्यवस्थित अध्ययन मंच का नेतृत्व किया था?
o: Tattvabodhini Sabha
Paramahansa Mandali
Satyashodhak Samaj
Social Service League
e: Detailed Explanation: Debendranath Tagore headed the Tattvabodhini Sabha (founded in 1839), which along with its organ Tattvabodhini Patrika, was entirely devoted to the systematic study of India's past with a rational outlook.

qe: The dismissal of Keshab Chandra Sen from the office of acharya in 1865 by Debendranath Tagore led to an operational split in the Brahmo Samaj. What was the name of the new organization founded by Sen in 1866?
qh: देवेंद्रनाथ टैगोर द्वारा 1865 में केशव चंद्र सेन को आचार्य के पद से बर्खास्त करने के कारण ब्रह्म समाज में विभाजन हुआ। 1866 में सेन द्वारा स्थापित नए संगठन का क्या नाम था?
o: Brahmo Samaj of India
Adi Brahmo Samaj
Sadharan Brahmo Samaj
Prarthana Samaj
e: Detailed Explanation: Following the 1865 split, Keshab Chandra Sen and his progressive followers founded the 'Brahmo Samaj of India' in 1866, while Debendranath Tagore's conservative wing became known as the 'Adi Brahmo Samaj'.

qe: In 1878, a major split occurred within Keshab Chandra Sen's Brahmo Samaj of India, resulting in the creation of the Sadharan Brahmo Samaj. Who among the following leaders spearheaded this development?
qh: 1878 में, केशव चंद्र सेन के ब्रह्म समाज ऑफ इंडिया के भीतर एक बड़ा विभाजन हुआ, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप साधारण ब्रह्म समाज का गठन हुआ। निम्नलिखित में से किस नेता ने इस विकास का नेतृत्व किया था?
o: Ananda Mohan Bose, Shibchandra Deb, and Umesh Chandra Datta
Atmaram Pandurang and R.G. Bhandarkar
Dadoba Pandurang and Mehtaji Durgaram
Gopal Krishna Gokhale and N.M. Joshi
e: Detailed Explanation: Disgusted by Keshab's action of marrying his underage daughter using orthodox Hindu rituals, his progressive followers broke away to found the Sadharan Brahmo Samaj under the leadership of Ananda Mohan Bose, Shibchandra Deb, and Umesh Chandra Datta.

qe: The Prarthana Samaj, founded in Bombay in 1867 with the assistance of Keshab Chandra Sen, owed its widespread popularity and national character to the tireless efforts of which leader who joined it in 1870?
qh: 1867 में केशव चंद्र सेन की सहायता से बॉम्बे में स्थापित प्रार्थना समाज को व्यापक लोकप्रियता और राष्ट्रीय स्वरूप 1870 में शामिल होने वाले किस नेता के अथक प्रयासों के कारण मिला?
o: Mahadeo Govind Ranade
Atmaram Pandurang
Balshastri Jambhekar
Gopalhari Deshmukh
e: Detailed Explanation: Mahadeo Govind Ranade joined the Prarthana Samaj in 1870, and his extensive efforts elevated the society's activities, transforming it into an organization with an all-India character focused on social reforms.

qe: The radical intellectual trend of the late 1820s known as the 'Young Bengal Movement' was inspired by which foundational international event?
qh: 1820 के दशक के उत्तरार्ध के क्रांतिकारी बौद्धिक रुझान, जिसे 'यंग बंगाल आंदोलन' (Young Bengal Movement) के रूप में जाना जाता है, को किस मौलिक अंतर्राष्ट्रीय घटना से प्रेरणा मिली थी?
o: The French Revolution
The American War of Independence
The Industrial Revolution
The Unification of Italy
e: Detailed Explanation: Henry Vivian Derozio, an Anglo-Indian teacher at Hindu College, inspired his pupils to think freely by drawing deep structural inspiration from the radical ideals of the French Revolution.

qe: What primary operational limitation caused the radical Young Bengal Movement to achieve only limited success and fail to secure a long-term impact on the masses?
qh: किस प्राथमिक परिचालन सीमा के कारण क्रांतिकारी यंग बंगाल आंदोलन केवल सीमित सफलता प्राप्त कर सका और जनता पर दीर्घकालिक प्रभाव डालने में विफल रहा?
o: Their radicalism was bookish in character and they lacked any real organizational link with the masses
They strictly opposed the spread of modern Western physical sciences
They were legally barred from publishing journals by the colonial courts
They integrated fully with the conservative orthodox zamindars of Bengal
e: Detailed Explanation: The Derozians failed to build a lasting mass movement because their radical ideas were mostly bookish and lacked deep roots in prevailing social conditions. Additionally, they failed to rally any supporting classes, such as the peasantry.

qe: Pandit Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar became the principal of Sanskrit College in 1850. Which progressive structural reform did he implement to break the monopoly of scriptural knowledge?
qh: पंडित ईश्वर चंद्र विद्यासागर 1850 में संस्कृत कॉलेज के प्राचार्य बने। स्क्रिप्टुरल ज्ञान के एकाधिकार को तोड़ने के लिए उन्होंने कौन सा प्रगतिशील संरचनात्मक सुधार लागू किया?
o: He opened the enrollment of Sanskrit College to non-brahmins
He systematically banned the teaching of all traditional Vedic scripts
He restricted the study of Sanskrit solely to English administrative officers
He aligned the college platform exclusively with the orthodox Dharma Sabha
e: Detailed Explanation: Determined to break the traditional priestly monopoly over scriptural knowledge, Vidyasagar opened the Sanskrit College to non-brahmin students and introduced Western thought to enhance Sanskritic learning.

qe: Balshastri Jambhekar is widely celebrated as the father of Marathi journalism. Which pioneering newspaper did he launch in 1832 to advocate for social reforms?
qh: बालशास्त्री जांभेकर को व्यापक रूप से मराठी पत्रकारिता के जनक के रूप में मनाया जाता है। सामाजिक सुधारों की वकालत करने के लिए उन्होंने 1832 में कौन सा अग्रणी समाचार पत्र शुरू किया था?
o: Darpan
Digdarshan
Sudharak
Kesari
e: Detailed Explanation: Balshastri Jambhekar launched the newspaper 'Darpan' in 1832 to awaken public consciousness regarding critical social reforms like widow remarriage and a scientific approach to life.

qe: The secret reform society known as the 'Paramahansa Mandali', founded in Maharashtra in 1849, focused its core meetings primarily on breaking which social boundary?
qh: 1849 में महाराष्ट्र में स्थापित 'परमहंस मंडली' (Paramahansa Mandali) नामक गुप्त सुधार सभा ने अपनी बैठकों को मुख्य रूप से किस सामाजिक सीमा को तोड़ने पर केंद्रित किया?
o: Breaking rigid caste rules by consuming food cooked by lower-caste people
Enforcing strict alignment with Sanskritic text validation patterns
Banning the study of Western physical and social sciences entirely
Promoting absolute polytheism across local rural presences
e: Detailed Explanation: The primary objective of the founders of the Paramahansa Mandali (like Dadoba Pandurang) was to challenge rigid caste barriers. At their secret meetings, members deliberately consumed food prepared by lower-caste individuals to defy orthodox caste rules.

qe: Mahatma Jyotiba Phule organized a powerful structural movement against upper-caste domination and Brahminical supremacy in Maharashtra. Which society did he found in 1873 for this purpose?
qh: महात्मा ज्योतिबा फुले ने महाराष्ट्र में उच्च जाति के वर्चस्व और ब्राह्मणवादी सर्वोच्चता के खिलाफ एक शक्तिशाली आंदोलन का गठन किया। इस उद्देश्य के लिए उन्होंने 1873 में किस सभा की स्थापना की?
o: Satyashodhak Samaj
Paramahansa Mandali
Prarthana Samaj
Servants of India Society
e: Detailed Explanation: Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (Truth Seekers' Society) in 1873. Its leadership came from backward classes, aiming at complete social service and expanding education among lower castes and women.

qe: Which two remarkable literary works written by Mahatma Jyotiba Phule served as vital sources of ideological inspiration for the depressed communities?
qh: महात्मा ज्योतिबा फुले द्वारा लिखित कौन सी दो उल्लेखनीय साहित्यिक कृतियाँ पीड़ित और वंचित समुदायों के लिए वैचारिक प्रेरणा के महत्वपूर्ण स्रोत बनीं?
o: Sarvajanik Satyadharma and Gulamgiri
Darpan and Digdarshan
Sudharak and Kesari
Hitechhu and Satya Prakash
e: Detailed Explanation: Jyotiba Phule’s major publications, 'Sarvajanik Satyadharma' and 'Gulamgiri', provided powerful arguments against Sanskritic Hinduism and upper-caste exploitation, giving depressed classes a distinct identity.

qe: Gopalhari Deshmukh is highly celebrated in modern Indian history under which distinctive pen name, under which he authored social reform essays in the weekly 'Prabhakar'?
qh: गोपालहरि देशमुख आधुनिक भारतीय इतिहास में किस विशिष्ट उपनाम (pen name) से अत्यधिक प्रसिद्ध हैं, जिसके तहत उन्होंने साप्ताहिक 'प्रभाकर' में सामाजिक सुधार के निबंध लिखे थे?
o: Lokahitawadi
Mahatma
Acharya
Derozio
e: Detailed Explanation: Gopalhari Deshmukh wrote extensive rationalist essays on social equity and anti-caste themes under the pen name 'Lokahitawadi' in the prominent weekly newspaper Prabhakar.

qe: Gopal Ganesh Agarkar was a fierce advocate of human reason who co-founded Fergusson College. He also served as the first editor of which famous nationalist journal started by Lokmanya Tilak?
qh: गोपाल गणेश आगरकर मानव विवेक (human reason) के मुखर समर्थक थे, जिन्होंने फर्ग्यूसन कॉलेज की सह-स्थापना की थी। उन्होंने लोकमान्य तिलक द्वारा शुरू की गई किस प्रसिद्ध राष्ट्रवादी पत्रिका के पहले संपादक के रूप में भी कार्य किया?
o: Kesari
Sudharak
Darpan
Hitavada
e: Detailed Explanation: Gopal Ganesh Agarkar was the initial editor of Tilak's famous journal 'Kesari'. He later established his own periodical, 'Sudharak', to campaign more directly against untouchability and the caste system.

qe: The specialized organization 'Servants of India Society' was established in 1905 to train national missionaries for the selfless service of the country. Who was its founder?
qh: देश की निःस्वार्थ सेवा के लिए राष्ट्रीय मिशनरियों को प्रशिक्षित करने के लिए 1905 में 'सर्वेंट्स ऑफ इंडिया सोसाइटी' (Servants of India Society) नामक विशेष संगठन की स्थापना की गई थी। इसके संस्थापक कौन थे?
o: Gopal Krishna Gokhale
Mahadeo Govind Ranade
Narayan Malhar Joshi
Ananda Mohan Bose
e: Detailed Explanation: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in 1905 with the assistance of M.G. Ranade, preparing a dedicated cadre of workers to promote the welfare of Indian citizens through constitutional means.

qe: Narayan Malhar Joshi founded the Social Service League in Bombay to secure reasonable working and life conditions for the masses. Which pivotal national labor organization did he also establish in 1920?
qh: नारायण मल्हार जोशी ने जनता के लिए उचित कामकाजी और जीवन की स्थिति सुनिश्चित करने के लिए बॉम्बे में सोशल सर्विस लीग की स्थापना की। उन्होंने 1920 में किस महत्वपूर्ण राष्ट्रीय श्रम संगठन की भी स्थापना की थी?
o: All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC)
All India Kisan Sabha
Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha
Satyashodhak Labour Front
e: Detailed Explanation: Apart from his social welfare work with the Social Service League, Narayan Malhar Joshi was a key pioneer of the Indian labor movement and founded the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) in 1920.

qe: Raja Rammohan Roy's continuous battle against the practice of Sati culminated in a landmark legislative victory when the colonial government passed an official Regulation declaring the practice a crime. In which year was this Regulation passed?
qh: सती प्रथा के खिलाफ राजा राममोहन राय की निरंतर लड़ाई के परिणामस्वरूप एक ऐतिहासिक विधायी जीत मिली जब औपनिवेशिक सरकार ने इस प्रथा को अपराध घोषित करने वाला एक आधिकारिक नियम पारित किया। यह नियम किस वर्ष पारित किया गया था?
e: Detailed Explanation: Raja Rammohan Roy began his intense anti-sati struggle in 1818, citing sacred shastras to prove the practice lacked religious sanction. His crusade resulted in the historic Government Regulation of 1829, which officially criminalized Sati.

qe: To broadbase his educational reforms and select the best elements from different cultures, Raja Rammohan Roy established a specialized Vedanta College in 1825. What unique academic structure did this college offer?
qh: अपने शैक्षिक सुधारों को व्यापक बनाने और विभिन्न संस्कृतियों के सर्वोत्तम तत्वों को चुनने के लिए, राजा राममोहन राय ने 1825 में एक विशेष वेदांत कॉलेज की स्थापना की। इस कॉलेज ने कौन सी अनूठी शैक्षणिक संरचना की पेशकश की थी?
o: Courses offering a blend of both traditional Indian learning and Western physical and social sciences
An exclusive training module designed solely for Christian missionary conversions
A military tactics academy focused entirely on European mechanical warfare metrics
An institution dedicated strictly to the compilation of standard Bengali grammar books
e: Detailed Explanation: In 1825, Raja Rammohan Roy established the Vedanta College, which offered an integrated curriculum combining traditional Indian philosophies and learning with modern Western physical and social sciences.

qe: As an internationalist with a vision far beyond his times, Raja Rammohan Roy actively celebrated and championed global struggles for liberty and justice. Which historical international revolution did he explicitly support?
qh: अपने समय से कहीं आगे की सोच रखने वाले एक अंतरराष्ट्रीय स्तर के नेता के रूप में, राजा राममोहन राय ने स्वतंत्रता और न्याय के वैश्विक संघर्षों का सक्रिय रूप से समर्थन किया। उन्होंने किस ऐतिहासिक अंतर्राष्ट्रीय क्रांति का स्पष्ट रूप से समर्थन किया था?
o: The revolutions of Naples and Spanish America
The absolute expansion of the centralized Russian czarist borders
The industrial deployment of British absentee landlordism in Ireland
The localized military tracking loops executed by the Austrian empire
e: Detailed Explanation: Roy was a passionate internationalist who closely monitored global movements for liberty. He actively supported the revolutions in Naples and Spanish America, while vocally condemning the oppression of Ireland by absentee English landlords.

qe: Maharishi Debendranath Tagore revitalized the Brahmo Samaj by bringing followers from another influential cultural platform he headed. What was the name of the organ journal published by that platform in Bengali?
qh: महर्षि देवेंद्रनाथ टैगोर ने ब्रह्म समाज को एक और प्रभावशाली सांस्कृतिक मंच के अनुयायियों को लाकर पुनर्जीवित किया जिसका वे नेतृत्व करते थे। उस मंच द्वारा बंगाली में प्रकाशित होने वाली मुख्य पत्रिका का नाम क्या था?
o: Tattvabodhini Patrika
Darpan
Digdarshan
Sudharak
e: Detailed Explanation: Debendranath Tagore led the Tattvabodhini Sabha, which published the highly influential Bengali journal 'Tattvabodhini Patrika'. This publication focused on studying India's past with a rational outlook and propagating Rammohan Roy's ideas.

qe: Keshab Chandra Sen was instrumental in popularizing the Brahmo movement outside Bengal. However, a major internal split occurred in 1866, dividing the movement into two fronts. What were their respective names?
qh: केशव चंद्र सेन ने बंगाल के बाहर ब्रह्म आंदोलन को लोकप्रिय बनाने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई थी। हालाँकि, 1866 में एक बड़ा आंतरिक विभाजन हुआ, जिसने आंदोलन को दो मोर्चों में विभाजित कर दिया। उनके संबंधित नाम क्या थे?
o: The Brahmo Samaj of India led by Keshab Chandra Sen, and the Adi Brahmo Samaj led by Debendranath Tagore
The Sadharan Brahmo Samaj led by progressive followers, and the Paramahansa Sabha
The Prarthana Samaj of Bombay, and the secret Manav Dharma Sabha of western regions
The Tattvabodhini Sabha of Calcutta, and the Young Bengal Derozian student network
e: Detailed Explanation: In 1866, the Brahmo Samaj split into two organizations: Keshab Chandra Sen and his progressive followers established the 'Brahmo Samaj of India', while Debendranath Tagore's conservative group became known as the 'Adi Brahmo Samaj'.

qe: In 1910, which educational setup was founded in Lahore by the Dayal Singh Trust explicitly to implant and disseminate the structural ideas of the Brahmo movement in Punjab?
qh: 1910 में, पंजाब में ब्रह्म आंदोलन के संरचनात्मक विचारों को प्रसारित करने के लिए दयाल सिंह ट्रस्ट द्वारा लाहौर में किस शैक्षणिक संस्थान की स्थापना की गई थी?
o: Dayal Singh College
Fergusson College
Sanskrit College of Lahore
Hindu College of the North
e: Detailed Explanation: The Dayal Singh Trust sought to root the theological and progressive social ideas of the Brahmo movement in Punjab, leading to the formal establishment of Dayal Singh College at Lahore in 1910.

qe: The Prarthana Samaj, which focused on monotheism and relied heavily on education and persuasion over open confrontation with orthodoxy, was tightly attached to which cultural heritage of Maharashtra?
qh: प्रार्थना समाज, जो एकेश्वरवाद पर केंद्रित था और रूढ़िवादिता के साथ खुले टकराव के बजाय शिक्षा और अनुनय पर बहुत अधिक निर्भर था, महाराष्ट्र की किस सांस्कृतिक विरासत से निकटता से जुड़ा था?
o: The traditional Bhakti cult of Maharashtra
The aggressive political tracking loops of local zamindars
The insular secret protocols of the Paramahansa Mandali
The early translation models of ancient Sanskrit dictionaries
e: Detailed Explanation: Unlike some radical movements, the Prarthana Samaj in Bombay maintained deep connections with popular local traditions, remaining closely attached to the legacy and devotional ethos of the Bhakti cult of Maharashtra.

qe: As a key government inspector of schools in the mid-19th century, Pandit Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar organized thirty-five girls' schools in Bengal. How were these specialized schools funded and sustained?
qh: 19वीं शताब्दी के मध्य में स्कूलों के एक प्रमुख सरकारी निरीक्षक के रूप में, पंडित ईश्वर चंद्र विद्यासागर ने बंगाल में पैंतीस लड़कियों के स्कूलों का आयोजन किया। इन विशेष स्कूलों को कैसे वित्तपोषित (funded) और संचालित किया गया था?
o: Many of them were run and sustained entirely at his own personal expense
They were funded fully by the conservative orthodox Dharma Sabha organization
They relied strictly on financial grants channeled from the Colaba Observatory
They were sustained by a specialized land revenue tax imposed on local ryots
e: Detailed Explanation: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a passionate advocate for female literacy. In addition to organizing public schools, he personally funded and sustained many of the thirty-five girls' schools he helped establish in Bengal.

qe: Balshastri Jambhekar launched the periodical 'Digdarshan' in 1840 to awaken public interest and broaden the scientific baseline of the masses. What specific content did this periodical publish?
qh: बालशास्त्री जांभेकर ने जनता की रुचि जगाने और उनके वैज्ञानिक आधार को व्यापक बनाने के लिए 1840 में 'दिग्दर्शन' (Digdarshan) पत्रिका शुरू की। इस पत्रिका ने कौन सी विशिष्ट सामग्री प्रकाशित की थी?
o: Articles explicitly covering scientific subjects as well as history
The legal transcripts of judicial decisions passed by British judges
Poetical compilations focused entirely on the French Revolution
A running ledger tracking the maximum rents fixed for local zamindars
e: Detailed Explanation: Following his success with the newspaper Darpan, Balshastri Jambhekar started 'Digdarshan' in 1840, a monthly periodical dedicated to popularizing historical knowledge and articles on various scientific subjects.

qe: Mahatma Jyotiba Phule implemented a powerful alternative tracking symbol to unify and inspire the backward common masses against upper-caste domination. Which ideological symbol did he choose?
qh: महात्मा ज्योतिबा फुले ने उच्च जाति के वर्चस्व के खिलाफ पिछड़े और आम जनमानस को एकजुट और प्रेरित करने के लिए एक शक्तिशाली वैकल्पिक प्रतीक लागू किया। उन्होंने किस वैचारिक प्रतीक को चुना?
o: The symbol of Rajah Bali, as opposed to the orthodox symbol of Rama
The alignment of the French Revolution's liberty rings
The physical structural layout of the Colaba Observatory lines
The traditional monotheistic icons derived from the Bhakti cult
e: Detailed Explanation: To construct an alternative cultural narrative challenging Brahminical supremacy, Jyotiba Phule rejected orthodox symbols and utilized the historical symbol of 'Rajah Bali' to rally and unify the lower strata of society.

qe: Swami Vivekananda established the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897 to institutionalize practical spirituality and humanitarian work. In which year did he formally acquire the large piece of land at Belur where the Ramakrishna Math was finally shifted and registered?
qh: स्वामी विवेकानंद ने व्यावहारिक आध्यात्मिकता और मानवीय कार्यों को संस्थागत रूप देने के लिए 1897 में रामकृष्ण मिशन की स्थापना की थी। उन्होंने किस वर्ष बेलूर में वह बड़ी भूमि औपचारिक रूप से अधिग्रहित की थी जहाँ रामकृष्ण मठ को अंततः स्थानांतरित और पंजीकृत किया गया था?
e: Detailed Explanation: Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897. A year later, in 1898, he acquired a large piece of land at Belur near Calcutta, where the twin organization, Ramakrishna Math, was permanently shifted and legally registered.

qe: Unlike certain contemporary socio-religious movements, the Ramakrishna Mission successfully broadbased its appeal across India. What structural feature contributed to its widespread institutional success?
qh: कुछ समकालीन सामाजिक-धार्मिक आंदोलनों के विपरीत, रामकृष्ण मिशन ने पूरे भारत में अपने आकर्षण को सफलतापूर्वक व्यापक बनाया। इसकी व्यापक संस्थागत सफलता में किस संरचनात्मक विशेषता ने योगदान दिया?
o: It organized strictly as a highly political proselytizing body
It did not consider itself a closed sect of Hinduism and recognized the psychological utility of image worship
It completely rejected any integration of modern Western physical sciences
It limited its institutional operations and schools exclusively to the city of Calcutta
e: Detailed Explanation: The Ramakrishna Mission succeeded because it chose not to operate as a proselytizing body or an exclusive sect of Hinduism. Unlike the Arya Samaj, it recognized the psychological value of image worship in developing spiritual fervor while applying practical Vedanta principles to solve social problems.

qe: The founder of the Arya Samaj, Swami Dayananda Saraswati, was born as Mulshankar in a Brahmin family. Which princely state in Gujarat was his birthplace?
qh: आर्य समाज के संस्थापक, स्वामी दयानंद सरस्वती का जन्म एक ब्राह्मण परिवार में मूलशंकर के रूप में हुआ था। गुजरात की कौन सी रियासत उनका जन्मस्थान थी?
o: Morvi
Baroda
Junagadh
Rajkot
e: Detailed Explanation: Swami Dayananda Saraswati (Mulshankar) was born in 1824 in the old Morvi princely state located in the Kathiawar region of Gujarat.

qe: Swami Dayananda Saraswati formally established the very first institutional unit of the Arya Samaj in April 1875 at which city before shifting its corporate headquarters to Lahore?
qh: स्वामी दयानंद सरस्वती ने अपने कॉर्पोरेट मुख्यालय को लाहौर स्थानांतरित करने से पहले अप्रैल 1875 में किस शहर में आर्य समाज की पहली संस्थागत इकाई औपचारिक रूप से स्थापित की थी?
o: Bombay
Ahmedabad
Mathura
Amritsar
e: Detailed Explanation: Swami Dayananda Saraswati formally set up the first unit of the Arya Samaj at Bombay in 1875. The headquarters of the socio-religious movement were subsequently shifted and established at Lahore.

qe: In his famous treatise 'Satyarth Prakash' (The True Exposition), Swami Dayananda Saraswati outlined his socio-religious vision. What did this vision fundamentally include?
qh: अपने प्रसिद्ध ग्रंथ 'सत्यार्थ प्रकाश' में स्वामी दयानंद सरस्वती ने अपने सामाजिक-धार्मिक दृष्टिकोण की रूपरेखा तैयार की थी। इस दृष्टिकोण में मौलिक रूप से क्या शामिल था?
o: A classless and casteless society, a united India, and freedom from foreign rule with Vedic alignment
A complete legal endorsement of the later Puranic scriptures and idol worship
The static retention of hereditary untouchability parameters across all provinces
A total structural alignment with British political administrative patronage channels
e: Detailed Explanation: 'Satyarth Prakash' advocated for a casteless and classless Indian society, a religiously, socially, and nationally unified India free from foreign colonial rule, based on the infallible authority of the original Vedas.

qe: From which blind Vedic scholar in Mathura did Swami Dayananda Saraswati receive his core spiritual education on Vedanta and scriptural purity?
qh: स्वामी दयानंद सरस्वती ने मथुरा में किस अंधे वैदिक विद्वान से वेदांत और शास्त्रीय शुद्धता पर अपनी मूल आध्यात्मिक शिक्षा प्राप्त की थी?
o: Swami Virajananda
Shiv Narayan Agnihotri
Radhakant Deb
Swami Shraddhanand
e: Detailed Explanation: Swami Dayananda Saraswati wandered as an ascetic for fifteen years before receiving his definitive scriptural education on Vedic purity from the blind scholar Swami Virajananda in Mathura.

qe: Swami Dayananda Saraswati launched a frontal attack on orthodox fatalism by explicitly rejecting which prevalent popular socio-philosophic belief?
qh: स्वामी दयानंद सरस्वती ने किस प्रचलित लोकप्रिय सामाजिक-दार्शनिक विश्वास को स्पष्ट रूप से खारिज करके रूढ़िवादी भाग्यवाद पर सीधा प्रहार किया?
o: The escapist interpretation of total dependence on niyati (destiny) and world-renunciation for salvation
The structural validity of the original four-fold chaturvarna classification based on merit
The operational implementation of women's tertiary educational frameworks
The physical thermodynamic theory of karma and systemic reincarnation wheels
e: Detailed Explanation: Dayananda strongly rejected the escapist Hindu belief that looked upon the world as mere maya (illusion) and niyati (destiny). He argued that God, soul, and prakriti are distinct eternal entities, and every individual must actively work for the well-being of others to attain salvation.

qe: How did the Arya Samaj structurally redefine the Vedic concept of the 'chaturvarna' system to counter the rigid hereditary caste distinctions?
qh: आर्य समाज ने रूढ़िवादी वंशानुगत जातिगत भेदभावों का मुकाबला करने के लिए 'चातुर्वर्ण्य' व्यवस्था की वैदिक अवधारणा को संरचनात्मक रूप से कैसे पुनर्परिभाषित किया?
o: By maintaining that a person's varna is determined strictly by occupation and merit rather than by birth
By totally abolishing the lower text scripts while retaining priestly dominance channels
By adding an artificial fifth tier exclusively for non-Asian foreign settlers
By forcing all trading classes to transform into landless agricultural ryots
e: Detailed Explanation: Swami Dayananda attacked hereditary caste rigidities by advocating for the original Vedic chaturvarna model. Under this layout, a person's social grouping as a Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, or Shudra was designated based entirely on their dynamic occupation and intellectual merit, not by birth.

qe: In its comprehensive charter for social reform, what minimum marriageable age parameters were systematically fixed by the Arya Samaj for boys and girls?
qh: सामाजिक सुधार के अपने व्यापक चार्टर में, आर्य समाज द्वारा लड़कों और लड़कियों के लिए न्यूनतम विवाह योग्य आयु के क्या मानक व्यवस्थित रूप से तय किए गए थे?
o: Twenty-five years for boys and sixteen years for girls
Eighteen years for boys and fourteen years for girls
Twenty-one years for boys and १८ years for girls
Twenty years for boys and fifteen years for girls
e: Detailed Explanation: To eradicate child marriage, the Arya Samaj laid down strict guidelines fixing the minimum marriageable age threshold at twenty-five years for males and sixteen years for females.

qe: Following the death of Swami Dayananda in 1883, the Arya Samaj experienced an internal schism in 1893. What were the two factions that split over educational curriculum and diet restrictions?
qh: 1883 में स्वामी दयानंद की मृत्यु के बाद, 1893 में आर्य समाज में एक आंतरिक विभाजन हुआ। पाठ्यक्रम और आहार प्रतिबंधों को लेकर विभाजित होने वाले दो गुट कौन से थे?
o: The College Party (favoring English and modern sciences) and the Mahatma Party (favoring Sanskrit and Gurukul traditions)
The Atmiya Sabha and the Dharma Sabha orthodox coalition
The Adi Arya Samaj and the Sadharan Prarthana wing
The Wahabi revivalist corps and the Aligarh modernist league
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1893 split divided the Arya Samaj into the College (or Culture) Party led by Lala Hansraj and Lala Lajpat Rai (who supported western English curriculum to meet professional needs), and the Mahatma (or Gurukul) Party led by Swami Shraddhanand (who advocated for Vedic philosophy and strict vegetarianism).

qe: In 1902, the Mahatma Party of the Arya Samaj permanently established the historic 'Gurukul Kangri' near Haridwar. What was the primary educational objective of this institution?
qh: 1902 में, आर्य समाज के महात्मा गुट ने हरिद्वार के पास ऐतिहासिक 'गुरुकुल कांगड़ी' की स्थापना की थी। इस संस्थान का प्राथमिक शैक्षिक उद्देश्य क्या था?
o: To provide an indigenous educational alternative to Lord Macaulay’s policy by focusing on Vedic literature, Indian philosophy, and modern sciences
To train exclusive groups of military commandos for the British East India Company
To serve as a high-cost bilingual accounting center for local zamindars
To exclusively translate Puranic literature into European classical languages
e: Detailed Explanation: Founded by Swami Shraddhanand, Gurukul Kangri aimed to counter Lord Macaulay's education policy by offering a structured indigenous alternative that combined deep studies in Vedic literature and Indian philosophy with modern scientific research.

qe: The Arya Samaj initiated the controversial 'shuddhi' (purification) movement during the early 20th century. What was the operational goal of this movement?
qh: आर्य समाज ने 20वीं शताब्दी की शुरुआत में विवादास्पद 'शुद्धि' (purification) आंदोलन शुरू किया था। इस आंदोलन का परिचालन लक्ष्य क्या था?
o: To reconvert individuals who had converted to Christianity or Islam back into the Hindu fold
To extract all heavy magnesium and calcium minerals from local village community wells
To systematically purge modern Western scientific subjects from the D.A.V. College curriculum
To legally dissolve all inter-caste marriage contracts registered inside the Punjab province
e: Detailed Explanation: The Shuddhi movement was launched as a defensive and revivalist mechanism to protect Hindu society. It aimed at reconverting former Hindus who had embraced Islam or Christianity back to the Hindu fold, while also working to integrate untouchables into pure caste Hindu structures.

qe: The Parsi social reformer Behramji M. Malabari founded the 'Seva Sadan' in 1908 alongside which of his close associates?
qh: पारसी सामाजिक सुधारक बेहरामजी एम. मालाबारी ने 1908 में अपने किस करीबी सहयोगी के साथ मिलकर 'सेवा सदन' (Seva Sadan) की स्थापना की थी?
o: Diwan Dayaram Gidumal
Shiv Narayan Agnihotri
Radhakant Deb
Narayan Malhar Joshi
e: Detailed Explanation: Behramji M. Malabari, a relentless Parsi crusader against child marriage, established the Seva Sadan in 1908 in collaboration with Diwan Dayaram Gidumal to specialize in the care, welfare, and medical rehabilitation of exploited and destitute women.

qe: Which specific weekly journal was acquired and edited by the prominent social reformer Behramji M. Malabari to propagate his progressive social ideas and push for the Age of Consent Act?
qh: बाल विवाह के खिलाफ अपने विचारों को प्रसारित करने के लिए प्रमुख सामाजिक सुधारक बेहरामजी एम. मालाबारी द्वारा किस साप्ताहिक पत्रिका का संपादन किया गया था?
o: The Indian Spectator
Rast Goftar
Tahdhib-ul-Akhlaq
Hitavada
e: Detailed Explanation: Behramji M. Malabari acquired and effectively edited 'The Indian Spectator', using its media platform to advocate relentlessly for women's rights, child marriage restrictions, and widow remarriage.

qe: The 'Dev Samaj', founded at Lahore in 1887 by Shiv Narayan Agnihotri, compiled its primary ethical principles and teachings into which sacred text?
qh: शिव नारायण अग्निहोत्री द्वारा 1887 में लाहौर में स्थापित 'देव समाज' ने अपने प्राथमिक नैतिक सिद्धांतों और शिक्षाओं को किस ग्रंथ में संकलित किया था?
o: Deva Shastra
Satyarth Prakash
Tahdhib-ul-Akhlaq
Maktubat-i-Sadi
e: Detailed Explanation: The Dev Samaj emphasized moral code, ideal social behavior (such as refusing bribes and keeping away from non-vegetarian food), and the supremacy of the guru. Its complete spiritual tenets were compiled in the book 'Deva Shastra'.

qe: In 1830, Radhakant Deb founded the Dharma Sabha. What was the central ideological stance of this conservative organization regarding socio-religious legislation like the abolition of Sati?
qh: 1830 में राधाकांत देव ने धर्म सभा की स्थापना की थी। सती प्रथा के उन्मूलन जैसे सामाजिक-धार्मिक कानूनों के संबंध में इस रूढ़िवादी संगठन का केंद्रीय वैचारिक रुख क्या था?
o: It stood for the preservation of the status quo and strongly opposed the legal abolition of Sati
It launched an aggressive armed rebellion against the introduction of Western female education
It demanded the immediate dissolution of all priestly monopolies over scriptural knowledge
It advocated for a casteless and classless alignment across the Bengal Presidency
e: Detailed Explanation: The Dharma Sabha was explicitly formed as an orthodox backlash against Raja Rammohan Roy's progressive campaigns. It stood for the strict preservation of status quo in socio-religious matters, going so far as to formally petition against the legal abolition of Sati, though it favored Western education for girls.

qe: In 1902, several conservative organizations—including the Sanatana Dharma Sabha (1895) and the Dharma Maha Parishad—merged to form a unified front called 'Bharat Dharma Mahamandala'. Where was its permanent corporate headquarters established?
qh: 1902 में, सनातन धर्म सभा (1895) और धर्म महा परिषद सहित कई रूढ़िवादी संगठन आपस में मिलकर 'भारत धर्म महामण्डल' बने। इसका स्थायी मुख्यालय कहाँ स्थापित किया गया था?
o: Varanasi
Calcutta
Lahore
Bombay
e: Detailed Explanation: To construct a unified pan-Indian defense of traditional orthodox Hinduism against the reformist onslaught of the Arya Samaj and the Ramakrishna Mission, these groups combined in 1902 to establish the Bharat Dharma Mahamandala with headquarters at Varanasi, under leaders like Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya.

qe: The Radhaswami Movement, which prioritized a simple social life, the company of pious people (satsang), and the supremacy of the guru without demanding worldly renunciation, was founded in 1861 at Agra by whom?
qh: राधास्वामी आंदोलन (Radhaswami Movement), जो सांसारिक संन्यास की मांग किए बिना एक सरल सामाजिक जीवन और गुरु की सर्वोच्चता को प्राथमिकता देता था, की स्थापना 1861 में आगरा में किसके द्वारा की गई थी?
o: Tulsi Ram (Shiv Dayal Saheb)
Shiv Narayan Agnihotri
Mohammad Qasim Nanotavi
Mirza Ghulam Ahmad
e: Detailed Explanation: Tulsi Ram, a prominent banker from Agra popularly known as Shiv Dayal Saheb, founded the Radhaswami sect in 1861. The movement discarded temple visits and shrines, emphasizing personal faith, internal prayer, and works of active charity.

qe: The historic Sree Narayana Guru Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Movement emerged in Kerala out of a structural conflict between upper castes and the Ezhavas. What was the traditional occupational profile of the Ezhavas?
qh: केरल में श्री नारायण गुरु धर्म परिपालन (SNDP) आंदोलन उच्च जातियों और एझावा समुदाय के बीच एक संरचनात्मक संघर्ष से उभरा था। एझावा समुदाय का पारंपरिक व्यावसायिक प्रोफ़ाइल क्या था?
o: A backward caste of toddy-tappers who were treated as untouchables
A wealthy land-owning intermediate merchant class
A scholarly network of high-caste temple priests
A nomadic warrior group working inside princely military circles
e: Detailed Explanation: The Ezhavas were the single largest caste group in Kerala (constituting 26% of the population) but were historically treated as untouchables, subjected to severe social disabilities, and denied temple entry. Their traditional occupation was toddy-tapping.

qe: In 1888, Sree Narayana Guru initiated a quiet revolution against upper-caste monopoly by installing a stone taken from the Neyyar river as a Sivalinga on Sivaratri. Where did this historic consecration take place?
qh: 1888 में, श्री नारायण गुरु ने शिवरात्रि पर नेय्यार नदी से लिए गए एक पत्थर को शिवलिंग के रूप में स्थापित करके उच्च जाति के एकाधिकार के खिलाफ एक मूक क्रांति शुरू की थी। यह ऐतिहासिक प्रतिष्ठापन कहाँ हुआ था?
o: Aruvippuram
Vaikom
Guruvayur
Travancore
e: Detailed Explanation: Sree Narayana Guru performed this historic consecration at Aruvippuram in 1888 to explicitly show that ritual installation and devotion were not the monopoly of higher castes. This structural breakthrough launched the Aruvippuram Movement.

qe: When the Aruvippuram Sree Narayana Guru Dharma Paripalana Yogam (SNDP) was formally registered as a large organization in 1903 under the Indian Companies Act, who served as its first General Secretary?
qh: जब अरुविप्पुरम श्री नारायण गुरु धर्म परिपालन योगम (SNDP) को 1903 में भारतीय कंपनी अधिनियम के तहत औपचारिक रूप से एक बड़े संगठन के रूप में पंजीकृत किया गया था, तो इसके पहले महासचिव के रूप में किसने कार्य किया था?
o: Kumaran Asan
Dr. Palpu
T.K. Madhavan
K.P. Kesava
e: Detailed Explanation: Registered in 1903 with the critical organizational support of Dr. Palpu, the SNDP Yogam had Sree Narayana Guru as its permanent chairman, while the famous romantic poet Kumaran Asan served as its first general secretary.

qe: The Justice Movement, launched in the Madras Presidency during the early 20th century to secure jobs and representation for non-Brahmins in the legislature, was led by which triad of leaders?
qh: 20वीं शताब्दी की शुरुआत में मद्रास प्रेसीडेंसी में गैर-ब्राह्मणों के लिए नौकरियों और विधायिका में प्रतिनिधित्व सुरक्षित करने के लिए शुरू किए गए 'जस्टिस मूवमेंट' (Justice Movement) का नेतृत्व किस त्रिमूर्ति द्वारा किया गया था?
o: C.N. Mudaliar, T.M. Nair, and P. Tyagaraja
E.V. Ramaswamy Naicker, K. Kelappan, and A.K. Gopalan
Sri Narayana Guru, Kumaran Asan, and Dr. Palpu
Naoroji Furdonji, Dadabhai Naoroji, and S.S. Bengalee
e: Detailed Explanation: The Justice Movement was started by C.N. Mudaliar, T.M. Nair, and P. Tyagaraja in Madras Presidency. Their efforts directly led to the formation of the Madras Presidency Association in 1917, which demanded definitive legislative quotas for lower castes.

qe: In the mid-1920s, E.V. Ramaswamy Naicker launched the Self-Respect Movement in South India. What unique tactical step did he introduce to directly undermine the authority of Brahmin priests?
qh: 1920 के दशक के मध्य में, ई.वी. रामास्वामी नायकर ने दक्षिण भारत में आत्म-सम्मान आंदोलन (Self-Respect Movement) शुरू किया। ब्राह्मण पुजारियों के अधिकार को कम करने के लिए उन्होंने कौन सा अनूठा कदम उठाया?
o: Formalizing and organizing weddings completely without the presence of Brahmin priests
Banning all lower-caste members from traveling outside municipal district boundaries
Petitioning the British Raj to completely dissolve the High Court Judicial branches
Forcing all non-Brahmin intermediate castes to strictly adopt Sanskritic ritual habits
e: Detailed Explanation: E.V. Ramaswamy Naicker (Periyar) aimed to reject Brahminical religion and culture as tools of exploitation. To challenge this system directly, his movement promoted and formalized 'self-respect marriages' executed completely without the intervention of Brahmin priests.

qe: The Vaikom Satyagraha was launched in Kerala in 1924 as a major milestone in the anti-caste movement. What was the central demand of this satyagraha?
qh: केरल में 1924 में शुरू किया गया 'वायकोम सत्याग्रह' (Vaikom Satyagraha) जाति-विरोधी आंदोलन में एक बड़ा मील का पत्थर था। इस सत्याग्रह की मुख्य मांग क्या थी?
o: Throwing open the roads and entry of Hindu temples surrounding Vaikom to the untouchables
Demanding complete exemption of local ryots from paying heavy land revenue tax streams
The immediate standard implementation of English-medium curriculum across all Khalsa schools
A total ban on the operational entry of Christian missionaries inside Travancore borders
e: Detailed Explanation: Launched in 1924 under the leadership of K.P. Kesava, the Vaikom Satyagraha was a highly disciplined non-violent agitation demanding that the public roads leading to the temple at Vaikom be opened to lower-caste untouchables. It was heavily supported by Mahatma Gandhi and volunteer jathas.

qe: Following prolonged agitations, on November 12, 1936, a historic Proclamation was issued that threw open all government-controlled temples to all Hindus regardless of caste. Which princely state ruler issued this Proclamation?
qh: लंबे आंदोलनों के बाद, 12 नवंबर, 1936 को एक ऐतिहासिक घोषणा (Proclamation) जारी की गई जिसने जाति की परवाह किए बिना सभी सरकारी नियंत्रित मंदिरों को सभी हिंदुओं के लिए खोल दिया। यह घोषणा किस रियासत के शासक ने जारी की थी?
o: The Maharaja of Travancore
The Ruler of Indore State
The Maharaja of Kolhapur
The Nizam of Hyderabad
e: Detailed Explanation: Decades of sustained temple entry movements led by social reformers culminated in a historic legal victory on November 12, 1936, when the Maharaja of Travancore issued a structural proclamation throwing open all state-controlled temples to all caste configurations.

qe: The 'Indian Social Conference', which functioned effectively as the specialized social reform cell of the Indian National Congress, was founded in 1887 by which leaders?
qh: भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस के सामाजिक सुधार प्रकोष्ठ (social reform cell) के रूप में कार्य करने वाले 'भारतीय सामाजिक सम्मेलन' (Indian Social Conference) की स्थापना 1887 में किन नेताओं द्वारा की गई थी?
o: M.G. Ranade and Raghunath Rao
Gopal Krishna Gokhale and Srinivasa Shastri
Atmaram Pandurang and Dadoba Pandurang
Ananda Mohan Bose and Lala Lajpat Rai
e: Detailed Explanation: Founded by Mahadeo Govind Ranade and Raghunath Rao, the Indian Social Conference held its inaugural session in Madras in 1887. It met annually at the same time and venue as the INC, launching the famous 'Pledge Movement' against child marriage.

qe: The revivalist Wahabi or Walliullah Movement of the 18th century was built on the ideals of Shah Walliullah. What was his specific stance regarding Muslim jurisprudence?
qh: 18वीं शताब्दी का पुनरुत्थानवादी वहाबी या वलीउल्लाह आंदोलन (Wahabi Movement) शाह वलीउल्लाह के विचारों पर आधारित था। मुस्लिम न्यायशास्त्र (jurisprudence) के संबंध में उनका विशिष्ट रुख क्या था?
o: Desirability of harmony and integration among the four competing schools of Muslim jurisprudence
The total legal rejection of individual conscience in interpreting the Quran and Hadis
An absolute structural alliance with the Sikh kingdom operating inside the Punjab region
The mandatory introduction of Western scientific subjects within local academic centers
e: Detailed Explanation: Shah Walliullah (1702–1763) aimed to unify Indian Muslims. He advocated for harmony among the four major schools of Islamic jurisprudence, which had deeply divided the community, and emphasized the role of individual conscience when conflicting scriptural interpretations arose.

qe: During the mid-19th century, the Wahabi Movement shifted its focus geographically. After the British annexed the Punjab in 1849, against whom was the movement primarily directed?
qh: 19वीं शताब्दी के मध्य के दौरान, वहाबी आंदोलन ने अपना ध्यान भौगोलिक रूप से स्थानांतरित कर दिया। 1849 में अंग्रेजों द्वारा पंजाब पर कब्जा करने के बाद, यह आंदोलन मुख्य रूप से किसके खिलाफ निर्देशित था?
o: The British Government and its military structures
The Sikh rulers of Lahore exclusively
The localized Faraizi peasant parameters of East Bengal
The non-proselytizing bodies of the Ramakrishna Mission
e: Detailed Explanation: Initially, the Wahabi political front was directed against the Sikh rule in Punjab. However, following the British annexation of Punjab in 1849, the movement focused entirely on resisting British colonial might, playing a key anti-British role during the 1857 Revolt before being suppressed in the 1870s.

qe: Mir Nithar Ali, popularly celebrated as Titu Mir, led a historic peasant movement in Bengal. Against which specific groups did he organize the local Muslim peasantry?
qh: मीर निथार अली, जिन्हें लोकप्रिय रूप से तीतू मीर (Titu Mir) के नाम से जाना जाता है, ने बंगाल में एक ऐतिहासिक किसान आंदोलन का नेतृत्व किया था। उन्होंने स्थानीय मुस्लिम किसानों को किन विशिष्ट समूहों के खिलाफ संगठित किया था?
o: The oppressive, mostly Hindu landlords and British indigo planters
The revivalist ulema networks operating inside Saharanpur
The Parsi corporate managers who published the Rast Goftar paper
The secular educational administrators of the Aligarh Muslim University
e: Detailed Explanation: Titu Mir, a dedicated disciple of Sayyid Ahmed Barelvi, adopted Wahabism and successfully organized the poor Muslim peasants of Bengal against the heavy exactions of local landlords (who were mostly Hindu) and British indigo planters, before being killed in action in 1831.

qe: The Faraizi Movement, founded by Haji Shariatullah in 1818 in East Bengal, underwent a revolutionary structural transformation from 1840 onwards under his son. What was his son's name?
qh: पूर्वी बंगाल में 1818 में हाजी शरियतमुल्लाह द्वारा स्थापित 'फराइजी आंदोलन' (Faraizi Movement) में 1840 के बाद से उनके बेटे के तहत एक क्रांतिकारी संरचनात्मक परिवर्तन हुआ। उनके बेटे का नाम क्या था?
o: Dudu Mian
Titu Mir
Syed Ahmed Barelvi
Mirza Ghulam Ahmad
e: Detailed Explanation: Under Haji Shariatullah's son, Dudu Mian, the Faraizi movement adopted a highly militant, revolutionary character from 1840 onward. He established a tiered organizational system with local deputies (khalifas), raised a club-wielding paramilitary force to fight landlords, established alternative courts, and ordered followers to refuse rent payments.

qe: The Ahmadiyya Movement, founded by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad in 1889, established a unique doctrinal profile among Islamic sects. What was a central belief of this movement?
qh: 1889 में मिर्ज़ा गुलाम अहमद द्वारा स्थापित 'अहमदिया आंदोलन' ने इस्लामी संप्रदायों के बीच एक अनूठा सैद्धांतिक प्रोफ़ाइल स्थापित किया। इस आंदोलन का केंद्रीय विश्वास क्या था?
o: It believed that the Messiah had come in the person of Mirza Ghulam Ahmad to end religious wars and reinstate peace, tolerance, and human rights
It strongly advocated for the mandatory launching of aggressive jihad against all non-Muslim setups
It strictly opposed the dissemination of Western liberal education or physical sciences among Muslims
It demanded the absolute merging of the local religious mosque structures with State administrative branches
e: Detailed Explanation: The Ahmadiyya movement was anchored on highly liberal, universal principles. It opposed jihad, favored the separation of mosque and state, promoted Western education, and believed that Mirza Ghulam Ahmad was the promised Messiah sent to end religious conflict and promote peace.

qe: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan was a prominent educational and social reformer who was knighted in 1888. In 1875, he established which landmark institution at Aligarh to introduce Western scientific education to Muslims?
qh: सर सैयद अहमद खान एक प्रमुख शैक्षिक और सामाजिक सुधारक थे जिन्हें 1888 में नाइटहुड की उपाधि दी गई थी। 1875 में, उन्होंने मुसलमानों के लिए पश्चिमी वैज्ञानिक शिक्षा शुरू करने के लिए अलीगढ़ में किस ऐतिहासिक संस्थान की स्थापना की थी?
o: Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College
Darul Uloom Islamic Center
Nadwatal Ulama Academy
Dayal Singh Trust College
e: Detailed Explanation: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan established the Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh in 1875.
